headline: Frost and patchy fog expected early Monday, then mostly dry and warming through Friday, with cooler, rainier weather likely by Saturday.
summary: Dry air from the northeast has kept skies clear, and that continues tonight. Clear skies and light winds should let temperatures drop quickly, so a Frost Advisory is in effect from midnight tonight to 8 AM Monday for much of the Puget Sound area southward, the Hood Canal, and the North Coast. Sensitive plants can be damaged, and forecasters say the advisory marks the end of the growing season in these areas. Patchy fog is possible early Monday, mainly in the southern interior and valleys. If temperatures reach freezing, it could be freezing fog, but forecasters are unsure how low temperatures will get. Highs Monday should climb a bit, with most inland areas topping 60 degrees. More clouds arrive Monday night as a weak atmospheric river (a narrow stream of moisture) aims at British Columbia. Most of its rain should stay north of the Canadian border, though some may clip the northwestern Olympic Peninsula and the northern interior on Tuesday, and the extra clouds may limit frost and fog early Tuesday. Wednesday looks mostly dry for most of the region, with the best rain chances again on the Olympic Peninsula and northern interior, though the moisture's path may shift. An upper-level ridge (a zone of high pressure aloft that brings warm, dry weather) builds Thursday and Friday, and warming may start as early as Wednesday. Highs should reach the upper 60s to lower 70s by Friday, with the upper 70s possible in some Cascade valleys, including the Highway 12 corridor. No daily records are expected. By Saturday the ridge shifts well to the east and a trough (a dip in the jet stream) develops over the Pacific Northwest, which will likely bring rain chances and cooler temperatures, though the details are uncertain.
changes: Earlier discussions had Friday highs in the mid 60s to mid 70s and a weakening warm front bringing only slight rain chances Friday night into Saturday. By afternoon and evening, forecasters described Friday highs as upper 60s to lower 70s and a Saturday trough likely bringing rain and cooler weather, with the Tuesday-Wednesday moisture track now a noted uncertainty.
